name: comp-379
title: Content Block Picker
description: A plus button beside a document title opens a menu for adding content. Five rows pair a bordered icon tile with a block type and a one-line description: text, quote, divider and two headings.
use: An editor needs a compact menu for inserting new content blocks by type.
avoid: Rows are packed into a narrow menu, so descriptions wrap and the icons crowd the text.
a11y: The plus has an aria-label and rows use menu semantics; icon tiles are hidden from screen readers while titles carry meaning. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A rounded dark card shows 'Untitled document' and a grey hint, with a round ghost plus button at the right. The open menu drops below: a small 'Add block' label, then five rows, each starting with a tiny bordered icon square and holding a bold type name over a faint description.
behaves: Clicking the plus opens the menu; hovering a row highlights it and choosing one closes the menu. The document does not change in this demo.
customise: The five block options, icons and descriptions are written in the file; wiring them to an editor means adding handlers.
weight: light: A small menu of five rows with static icons; nothing runs in the background.
demo: Card 'Untitled document' with 'Add a block to keep writing'; menu has Text, Quote, Divider, Heading 1 and Heading 2.
issues: The menu is narrow, so block descriptions wrap into cramped two-line rows.
Block choices are not wired to any editor action in the demo.
polishWhy: Clear icon-plus-label rows; the cramped narrow menu and wrapped hints hold it back.
